full_judgment:
Another decision in the case of Babul alias Abdul Majid Khan and others Vs. State reported in 42 DLR (AD) 186 may also be looked into in this connection, wherein it has been held: 

 Now, in the instant case it appears that the learned Sessions Judge due to lack of his basic knowledge of the administration of criminal justice absolutely upon misconception of law has used the statements of the first Information Report as a piece of substantive evidence to prove the alleged charge against the appellant and thereby has committed serious illegality in his impugned judgment. Now with regard to the utilisation of the statements of the witnesses under section 161 CrPC the learned Advocate for the appellant has cited some decisions one in the case of Nazir Hussain Vs. Muhammad Shafi and others reported in 17 DLR (SC) 40, wherein it has been held by their Lordships as follows: 

 The learned advocate has also referred to another decision in the case of Ansar Ali &others Vs. State reported in 35 DLR (AD) 303 which has been based on a number of other decisions and it has been observed in the said decision as follows. 

 Similar views have been expressed in some other decisions reported in the case of Abdul Hashem Vs. State reported in 20 DLR 834 and also in the case of Ekabbar Ali Vs. State reported in 22 DLR 620. So from the provisions of sections 16 and 162 CrPC and the decisions as quoted above, it is crystal clear that the learned Sessions Judge fell in grave error of law in relying on the statements of the witnesses under section 161 CrPC as evidence in some form or other to prove and support the prosecution case and thereby has caused a serious miscarriage of justice. We, therefore, find much force in the submissions of the learned advocate for the appellant. The learned Advocate for the State however on the fact of the above state of evidence in this case and the submissions made before the bar and the decisions cited above ultimately finds it extremely difficult to support the impugned judgment and order of the learned Sessions Judge though he earlier tried to support the same. For the reasons stated above, we are, therefore of the view that the impugned judgment convicting and sentencing the accused appellant is palpably bad and illegal and the same cannot be sustained in law as well as on facts and it is, in fact, a case of no legal evidence. The appellant is entitled to acquittal also on the ground of benefit of doubt.
